title: PraisonAI Claude GitHub Action -- T1059.004 unquoted PR branch name command injection
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-48168 (GHSA-xp85-6wwf-r67c,
CVSS 10.0 CRITICAL), a self-reported advisory for PraisonAI, a
multi-agent teams system.

Prior to 4.6.40, the bundled `.github/workflows/claude.yml` (job
`claude-response`) interpolated an attacker-controlled PR branch name
directly into an unquoted Bash `run:` block --
`git fetch origin pull/${{ github.event.issue.number }}/head:${{
steps.check_fork.outputs.pr_branch }}` -- with no validation that the
branch name is a plausible git ref. Additionally, the workflow triggered
on any `@claude` comment without checking
`github.event.comment.author_association`, so a fork contributor could
open a PR whose branch name contained shell metacharacters and simply
comment `@claude` to run it -- no trusted-collaborator gate. The
advisory's own proof-of-concept branch name
(`poc;mkdir${IFS}-p${IFS}/tmp/p0canary;cp${IFS}/bin/echo${IFS}/tmp/p0canary/gh;echo${IFS}/tmp/p0canary>>$GITHUB_PATH`)
uses `${IFS}` to smuggle spaces past naive filtering and writes to
`$GITHUB_PATH`, poisoning which binaries later privileged steps resolve
-- the job held `contents: write`, `pull-requests: write`, `issues:
write`, and `id-token: write`.

Same root shape as this corpus's existing GitHub Actions PR-content rules
(`observed_megalodon_github_actions_base64_payload_t1195_002`,
`observed_tanstack_pwn_request_actions_cache_poisoning_t1195_002`,
`observed_claude_code_action_mcp_json_pr_rce_t1195_002`) -- attacker PR
content reaching a privileged CI execution context -- but the specific
injection vector here is the branch NAME itself rather than a file the PR
ships, which is why it is filed under `execution` (T1059.004, command
interpreter abuse) rather than `initial_access`: the artifact under
attack is the shell interpreting the ref string, not a config file being
trusted.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (MervinPraison, via
GHSA and NVD), fixed in 4.6.40.
